data.title: Event Tracking
data.tagline: A record of a page action sent to an analytics tool when the action occurs
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish an action trigger, an event send, and platform receipt, then verify counts with repeated actions and a reset.
data.description: To count clicks on Start trial, a developer can create a start_trial event in the click handler and add parameters such as the page source. A click means the event was triggered; analytics code must still send it and the platform must receive it before it appears in a debug or real-time view. A received event does not mean the aggregated report is complete.

learning.assumes: You have seen analytics dashboards, or want to know whether a feature gets used.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish an action trigger, an event send, and platform receipt, then verify counts with repeated actions and a reset.

distinctions.label: Conversion funnel
distinctions.explanation: A funnel is an analysis view built from metrics; tracking is the first step that produces the data—no events, no funnel.

distinctions.label: A/B test
distinctions.explanation: An A/B test is an experiment method comparing two options; it relies on tracking data to decide which performs better.

explanation.title: Place events at key points
explanation.text: Write one line of recording code at key actions like button clicks and form submits, naming the action.

explanation.title: Records are sent when actions happen
explanation.text: After a click triggers an event, the analytics SDK handles sending; receipt in a debug view is evidence about the test path, not proof that reports are complete.

explanation.title: Repeat the check, then reset it
explanation.text: Click several times to see whether records follow the actions, then clear the test state and repeat. The manual send and receipt controls here are teaching simulations, not a claim that real SDKs require manual sending.

data.boundary: The page demo uses manual controls to separate trigger, send, and receipt; real SDKs typically send events according to their configuration. A debug view can help check test events arrived, but does not guarantee every user's event was sent or that aggregate metrics are updated. Event records show actions, not why people took them.

lessonPractice.title: You need the click count for Start trial. How do you check tracking from the action through platform receipt?

options.label: Configure an event and source parameter, click repeatedly, send the events, and verify receipt in a debug view
options.feedback: Correct. Check trigger, send, and receipt separately; repeat clicks to verify the count, then reset and run the check again.

options.label: Count clicks by watching the test page and enter them in the report
options.feedback: Watching does not create verifiable event records or confirm that sending and receipt work.

options.label: Count page views and use them as the button click count
options.feedback: Page views and button clicks are different events; page opens cannot stand in for click records.

data.agentPrompt: Add a start_trial event and page_source parameter to the Start trial button. For verification, click it repeatedly and check event trigger, send, and receipt in the debug view separately; reset the test state and run it again. Explain what the local simulation and real analytics SDK/platform each do. Do not change the button's appearance.
